medications.sig: Take 1 to 2 tablets by mouth up to 3 times daily as needed for knee pain. Max 3,000 mg per day

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Knees have been grumbling more since he started helping a friend move furniture in February, both sides, worse going downstairs. No swelling, locking or giving way. No falls. Hasn't taken anything.
BP check otherwise, feels well.

BP as charted. Knees: crepitus both, no effusion, no warmth, ligaments stable, ROM full but stiff at end range. Gait normal.

A/P
Knee OA, both - flare with activity. Acetaminophen 500 mg, 1-2 tabs up to TID prn, ceiling 3 g/day. Avoiding NSAIDs with the diuretic and his age. Quad strengthening handout. Call if not settling in a month.
HTN - fine on HCTZ.
RTC fall.

documents.body: Pt called (his spring visit was pushed by the pandemic). Says he's been worn out for about two months, not hungry, pants are loose. events.reason: Fatigue, weight loss, lightheaded on standing

orders.reason: Fatigue, weight loss, hyperpigmentation, low AM cortisol

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, high MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Masked visit, screened at door.

S: about 2 months of steadily worse fatigue and poor appetite. Down from 80 kg in the fall to 74 today without trying. Lightheaded when he stands quickly, never passed out. Has noticed his forearms look tanned though he's barely been outside since March, which bothers him as a puzzle more than a worry. No N/V/abd pain, no fever, no cough, no melena. Sleep ok. Mood flat but not depressed by his account, no change in voices or thinking, psychiatry phone visit last month fine. Same meds.

O: BP 104/62, well below his usual. Weight 74 kg. Thin, tired-appearing. Forearms diffusely darker than upper arms, oral mucosa looks pigmented on the inner cheeks. Lungs clear, heart regular, abdomen soft, nontender. No LAD. No edema.

A/P
Fatigue, weight loss, low BP with darkening of skin and mucosa - this picture worries me for primary adrenal insufficiency. Drawing CMP, CBC and an AM cortisol now (drawn 8:20). Will call him with the cortisol and get him into endocrinology quickly if low. Hold off on HCTZ change until labs back. Reviewed red flags: vomiting, fainting, confusion -> ED and tell them about this workup.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Called pt. AM cortisol 2.8 mcg/dL, very low for 8 a.m.; CMP and CBC otherwise unremarkable. Explained this points toward the adrenal glands not making enough cortisol and that he needs endocrinology soon. Spoke with endocrinology triage: new-patient slot June 1, with stimulation testing that morning; they asked that we not start steroids before the test unless he gets sicker. Pt and daughter (on speaker) understand ED precautions. Daughter will drive him.

events.reason: Fatigue, weight loss, hyperpigmentation; low AM cortisol

medications.sig: Take 2 tablets (20 mg) by mouth every morning and 1 tablet (10 mg) every evening

documents.title: Endocrinology consultation
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
Endocrinology consultation, date of service 06/01/2020. Received by fax 06/22.

Reason: low morning cortisol, referred by his primary care physician.

This 72-year-old man describes several months of increasing tiredness, reduced appetite and weight loss he did not intend. He feels faint on standing. His forearms have darkened although he has had little sun exposure this spring. He has hypertension on hydrochlorothiazide, schizophrenia on quetiapine, osteoarthritis and BPH treated by TURP in 2017. Aspirin 81 mg. NKDA. Former smoker.

Exam: BP 100/60. Diffuse hyperpigmentation over both forearms and on the buccal mucosa. Remainder unremarkable.

Data: CBC with eosinophils 23%. Cosyntropin 250 mcg IV: cortisol 2.6 mcg/dL at baseline and 4.1 mcg/dL at 60 minutes. Plasma ACTH 486 pg/mL.

Impression: primary adrenal insufficiency.

Plan: hydrocortisone 20 mg on waking and 10 mg in the late afternoon/evening; fludrocortisone 0.1 mg daily. Sick-day rules reviewed with patient and daughter: double the hydrocortisone for fever or significant illness, go to the ED for vomiting. Advised a medical alert bracelet. Follow-up here in 3 months and then yearly.

Allergies: NKDA.
cc: primary care

documents.author: pharmacy
documents.body: Fill history update from retail pharmacy: hydrocortisone 10 mg tablets #90 and fludrocortisone 0.1 mg tablets #30 dispensed 06/01/2020, prescriber endocrinology.

documents.title: Endocrinology update
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Called to check in after endocrinology. Pt says they did the stimulation test and told him his adrenal glands "aren't pulling their weight." Started hydrocortisone twice a day (2 tabs in the morning, 1 at supper) and fludrocortisone daily. Already a bit more appetite. Knows to double the dose if sick and go to the ED for vomiting. Med list updated per pharmacy fill; letter not yet received. Follow-up with PCP mid-July booked.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Six weeks into hydrocortisone and fludrocortisone. "Night and day." Eating normally, energy back to walking most mornings, lightheadedness gone. Forearms maybe a shade lighter, hard to say. Endocrinology letter now in the chart.
Taking hydrocortisone 20 on waking, 10 around 5 pm; fludro in the morning. Has a bracelet on order.

BP 128/78, back to his old range. Weight 76 kg, up 2.
Lungs clear, heart regular, no edema.

A/P
Primary adrenal insufficiency - responding well to replacement. BMP today for Na/K on fludrocortisone plus HCTZ. Endocrinology follow-up in September.
HTN - BP back to normal range on HCTZ, continue.
Reviewed sick-day doubling again; gave him a wallet card.
RTC fall (AWV).

documents.body:
Video AWV, pt at home with daughter helping with the tablet; identity verified, consent for telehealth given.
Doing well since adrenal replacement started. Saw endocrinology in September: no changes, yearly now (his report). No falls. Independent. Using a pill box with morning and evening rows for the hydrocortisone.
PHQ-2 0. Psychiatry by phone, stable.
Meds: hydrocortisone 20/10, fludrocortisone 0.1, HCTZ 25, quetiapine 200 qhs, ASA 81, acetaminophen prn.
Home BP cuff (daughter bought one): 120s-130s/70s.

Plan: in-person lab draw and flu shot next week. Annual labs incl. quetiapine monitoring. COVID precautions reviewed. RTC 6 months in person.

documents.title: COVID vaccine
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Should I be getting the COVID shot with my adrenal problem? My daughter signed me up at the senior center clinic for early February. Do I need to do anything with the hydrocortisone?

documents.title: RE: COVID vaccine
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Yes, please get it; your adrenal condition is a reason to, not against. Keep taking your usual doses. If you get feverish or achy afterward, use your sick-day rule (double the hydrocortisone for a day or two) and let us know.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
First in-person visit since fall. Vaccinated x2.
New: since around the holidays, slow to get started, weaker stream, feels he hasn't finished. Up once at night. No burning, no blood, no fever. Thinks it's "the prostate again," like before his surgery.
Adrenal: stable on replacement, endocrinology yearly.

Vitals as charted. Abd soft, nontender, bladder not palpable. Deferred DRE to urology at his preference.
UA dip in office negative; sent for formal UA.

A/P
Obstructive LUTS 4 years after TURP - likely regrowth. Back to urology (the group that did the TURP). UA, BMP.
Primary adrenal insufficiency - stable.
HTN - ok.
RTC after urology.

conditions.label: Benign prostatic hyperplasia with lower urinary tract symptoms

medications.sig: Take 1 capsule by mouth daily, 30 minutes after the evening meal

documents.title: Urology consultation
documents.author: urology
documents.body:
Urology office note, seen 6/11/2021, faxed 6/28.

Mr. Levine had a TURP with our group in 2017. For roughly six months he has had trouble starting his stream, a weaker flow and the sense that his bladder doesn't empty. No dysuria. He also carries a diagnosis of primary adrenal insufficiency, followed by endocrinology.

Abdomen soft, nontender, bladder not distended to palpation. DRE: prostate moderately enlarged, firm, nontender, no nodules.
Urinalysis unremarkable. Bladder scan post-void residual 150 mL.

Assessment: recurrent benign prostatic hyperplasia after TURP with obstructive symptoms.
Plan: tamsulosin 0.4 mg nightly after supper; warned about lightheadedness on standing, especially the first week. Recheck in 3 months by phone, sooner if unable to void.

Meds reviewed: hydrocortisone, fludrocortisone, hydrochlorothiazide, quetiapine, aspirin. Allergies: NKDA.

documents.title: Pill timing
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Urology gave me tamsulosin after supper. My evening hydrocortisone is also at supper. Is it all right to take them together or should I space them?

documents.title: RE: Pill timing
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Checked with the doctor: fine to take them at the same time. Keep the tamsulosin about half an hour after you eat, and stand up slowly in the evening.

documents.title: Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
AWV.
Stream better on tamsulosin, urology phone check in September fine per pt. Adrenal replacement unchanged, endocrinology yearly. Psych stable.
No falls. Independent, still drives in daytime. Daughter does the big grocery runs.
PHQ-2 0. Recall 3/3.

BP 148/88, higher than his usual; home readings he reports in the 140s. Weight 78 kg, back near baseline.
Heart RRR, lungs clear, no edema.

A/P
HTN - creeping up since the fludrocortisone started. Will recheck in a few months before adding anything; asked him to log home readings.
Recurrent BPH - on tamsulosin, better.
Primary adrenal insufficiency - stable.
Annual labs. Flu and COVID booster with nurse in October. RTC 4-5 months.
